actions-list.actionItem: The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 9600.
Considered under suspension of the rules.
Mr. Westerman moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill. H.R. 9600 — "To approve the location of a commemorative work for Thomas Paine, America's indispensable and unsung Founding Father."

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 8483.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Westerman moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 8483 — "To take certain land in the State of California into trust for the benefit of the Barona Group of Capitan Grande Band of Mission Indians of the Barona Reservation, California, and for other purposes."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 8195.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Westerman moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 8195 — "To require the Secretary of the Interior to develop regional management frameworks for the take of double-crested cormorants."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 7954.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Westerman moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill. H.R. 7954 — "To assist Tribal governments in the management of buffalo and buffalo habitat and the reestablishment of buffalo on Indian land."
The Speaker announced that votes on suspensions, if ordered, will be postponed until a time to be announced.
The House convened, returning from a recess continuing the legislative day of November 17.
The Speaker announced that the House do now recess. The next meeting is subject to the call of the Chair.

The House received a message from the Clerk. Pursuant to the permission granted in Clause 2(h) of Rule II of the Rules of the U.S. House of Representatives, the Clerk notified the House that he had received the following message from the Secretary of the Senate on November 16, 2026, at 4:44 p.m.: That the Senate passed S. 432, S. 1353, S. 2887, S. 3493, and H.R. 2400 amended.
The House proceeded with one minute speeches.
The Chair designated Mr. Espaillat to lead the Members in reciting the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.
The Speaker announced approval of the Journal.  Pursuant to clause 1, rule I, the Journal stands approved.
Today's prayer was offered by Rabbi Ari Berman, Yeshiva University, New York, New York.
The House convened, returning from a recess continuing the legislative day of November 17.
The Speaker announced that the House do now recess. The next meeting is scheduled for 2:00 P.M. today.
The House resumed with Morning-Hour Debate.
The House received a message from the Senate. The Senate passed S. 3296, H.R. 2302, and H.R. 7834.
The House proceeded with Morning-Hour Debate. At the conclusion of Morning-Hour, the House will recess until 2:00 p.m. for the start of legislative business.
The Speaker designated the Honorable Mike Bost to act as Speaker pro tempore for today.
The House convened, starting a new legislative day.
